asks.q: i know nothing about f1, start there
a: ok so 22 cars, lined up roughly in qualifying order, less any grid penalties
in a dry race everyone has to use two different tyre types, so everyone stops at least once
the whole sport is basically deciding WHEN to lose that time

asks.q: why is the start always so mad
a: cold tyres, cold brakes, full fuel tank and everybody going for the same gap
it's the only moment of the race where the whole field is that close

asks.q: does the start decide the race
a: more than anyone admits
track position is everything on most circuits, you lose places on lap 1 and you can spend a long time stuck behind someone slower

msgs: lap 2 was the busiest of the whole race

a: yeah, only moves made on track count here
swaps in the pit lane and stuff behind the safety car are left out

msgs: most of the stops came around lap 27
this is the bit TV makes look boring and where a lot gets decided

asks.q: why not just stop early every time
a: new tyres are quickest for the first few laps, then they start going off
stop too early and you're on worn rubber at the end with everyone hunting you. stop too late and someone's already jumped you
you pit before the guy ahead, do fast laps on new tyres while he's still out there on old ones
if it works he comes out behind you after his stop. you never passed him on track, you passed him in the pit lane
honestly not sure, the data only tells me he stopped, not why
teams give the detail later, if at all
nope, not today
